correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and quantifiers are explicit. Two independent cusp-code words plus the Griesmer bound give a two-dimensional code of weights 12 and 15; their nonzero local coordinates force a connected degree-nine Kummer cover and smooth local A2 universal covers. The fiber inertia lines have sizes 5,5,5,2; every cusp has three smooth preimages. Noether and codimension-one canonical pullback give K-square 45, Euler 87, chi 11. Tan’s exact theorem for 12- and 15-cusp intermediate cyclic quotients forces q zero and hence pg ten. Holomorphic Lefschetz Fourier inversion gives 4 invariant, six single and two missing canonical characters. The embedded exact checker was run from its current package source, and finite tests were not substituted for these general arguments.

originality.rationale: The full recent primary paper constructs the two-weight-twelve-code family but does not analyze its simultaneous smooth degree-nine cover, four inertia subgroups or canonical character representation. Tan supplies single-cyclic-cover ingredients and older code inequalities, while Rito (2016) covers a distinct triple-cover problem. Comparison of actual statements, not titles, and focused semantic/primary-literature searches found no covering result; a general abelian-cover reformulation remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Standard Kummer theory and Tan’s cyclic-cover results imply several intermediate steps. A specialized older general abelian-cover argument could implicitly entail the same character/fixed-point profile without mentioning this recent family.
